comments.content: 1. **`src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManagerLocal.cpp:101`** — Reinterpreting `shared_ptr<list<shared_ptr<ModelLibraryLocal>>>` as an unrelated `shared_ptr<list<shared_ptr<ModelLibrary>>>` is undefined behavior. Calling `getLibraries()` and iterating the returned list can be miscompiled or crash; mutating it can insert a base-only `ModelLibrary` into storage later treated as `ModelLibraryLocal`.

2. **`src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManagerExternal.cpp:52`** — `ModelCacheSize` is not validated before being passed to the LRU cache. With `ModelCacheSize=0`, the first successful model insertion attempts eviction from an empty zero-capacity cache, causing an assertion failure or invalid access; a negative value can convert to an enormous unsigned capacity.

3. **`src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManagerExternal.cpp:122`** — Cache accesses and mutations are unsynchronized despite the cache being static and the LRU implementation not being thread-safe. Two simultaneous `getModel()` calls, or `getModel()` concurrent with `addModel()`/`resetCache()`, can corrupt the cache’s map/list and crash.

4. **`src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManager.cpp:172`** — `getLibrary()` never catches `LibraryNotFound` from the external manager. With external mode enabled, requesting a local-only library such as `User` first queries the external service; when it reports “not found,” the exception escapes and the existing local library is never searched.

5. **`src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManager.cpp:210`** — `libraryModels()` does not catch `ConnectionError`. With external mode enabled but the service offline, requesting models from an entirely local library fails with a connection exception instead of returning its local models.

6. **`src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManager.cpp:272`** — The library-qualified `getModel(libraryName, uuid)` ignores `libraryName`. For `getModel("does-not-exist", validUuid)`, it returns an unrelated model instead of rejecting the nonexistent library; with UUID collisions, it can return a model from the wrong library.

7. **`src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManagerExternal.cpp:146`** — `getModels()` always returns an empty map. With external mode enabled and external models present, `ModelManager::getModels()` returns only local models, so searches and enumerations based on this API omit every external model.

8. **`src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManagerExternal.cpp:138`** — A transient `ConnectionError` is converted to `nullptr` and cached under the UUID. If the server is unavailable for one lookup and then recovers, all subsequent lookups remain cache hits on `nullptr`; callers receive a local same-UUID model or `ModelNotFound` without retrying the recovered service.

9. **`src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManager.cpp:121`** — `refresh()` refreshes only the local manager. If an external model changes, is added after a negative cache entry, or was cached during an outage, invoking the public refresh operation leaves the stale external cache untouched.

10. **`src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManager.cpp:111` and `src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManagerExternal.cpp:58`** — External cleanup is both unreachable after the unconditional `return` and implemented as a no-op. After `ModelManager::cleanup()`, cached external `shared_ptr<Model>` objects and their associated resources remain live and are returned by later lookups while local state has been cleared.

11. **`src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManager.cpp:138`** — External libraries are returned through the generic library list, but `renameLibrary`, `changeIcon`, and `removeLibrary` still operate only on `_localManager`. Applying any of these operations to an editable external library either reports it missing or, if a hidden local library has the same name, modifies the wrong local library.

12. **`src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManager.cpp:164`** — `createLibrary()` calls the external manager even when `_useExternal` is false. Creating `"MyLibrary"` with external support compiled but disabled writes it to the external backend, while `getLibraries()` continues hiding it, making the newly created library appear to have vanished.

13. **`src/Mod/Material/App/ModelLibrary.cpp:75`** — Tree construction resolves listings globally by library name. If local and external libraries are both named `"Shared"`, obtaining the local object through `getLocalLibraries()` and calling `getModelTree()` on it uses the external `"Shared"` listing and displays remote models instead of the local library’s contents.

14. **`src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManager.cpp:218`** — An `InvalidModel` from an external library is swallowed and replaced by a local lookup. If external `"Shared"` contains malformed model data and a local `"Shared"` also exists, selecting the external library silently displays the unrelated local models; without a local duplicate, the original corruption error is masked by `LibraryNotFound`.

15. **`src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManagerExternal.cpp:106`** — `getLibrary()` converts `ConnectionError` into `LibraryNotFound`. Requesting an existing remote library during an outage therefore reports that the library does not exist, preventing callers from distinguishing missing data from a retryable connection failure.

16. **`src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManager.cpp:231`** — `isLocalLibrary()` interprets the translated outage error as external absence and returns `true`. If the server drops while checking a known external library, the UI can classify it as local and enable filesystem-only operations for it.

17. **`src/Mod/Material/App/ModelLibrary.cpp:75`** — `getModelTree()` no longer reads the map populated by `ModelLibraryLocal::addModel()`. Creating a local library, calling `addModel(model, "Folder/x.yml")`, and then calling `getModelTree()` omits that model unless separate code also inserted it into the global manager map; previously the model appeared immediately.

18. **`src/Mod/Material/App/ModelLibrary.cpp:83`** — `QString::split("/")` retains empty components. A root model with `path=""`, or a model with `path="/Metals/"` or `"Metals//Steel"`, is placed beneath one or more blank folder nodes rather than at the intended location.

19. **`src/Mod/Material/App/ModelLibrary.cpp:104`** — Models are keyed only by `filename`, and assignment silently replaces an existing entry. If an external backend returns `(u1, "Metals", "Steel")` and `(u2, "Metals", "Steel")`, only the second model remains in the tree even though the UUIDs are distinct.

20. **`src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManagerExternal.cpp:157` and `src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManagerExternal.cpp:167`** — Both `addModel()` and `migrateModel()` dereference their nullable `shared_ptr<Model>` before handing it to the backend. Passing `nullptr` crashes at `model->getUUID()` instead of producing an API error.

21. **`src/Mod/Material/App/ModelManager.cpp:99`** — `_useExternal` is written by the parameter observer and read by lookup methods without synchronization. Changing the preference while a worker thread calls `getModel()` or `getLibraries()` creates a C++ data race with undefined behavior.

**1. ModelManagerLocal.cpp:101–103 — `reinterpret_cast` produces a bogus list pointer (UB).**
`getLibraries()` returns `reinterpret_cast<std::shared_ptr<std::list<std::shared_ptr<ModelLibrary>>>&>(_libraryList)`, where `_libraryList` is a `std::list<std::shared_ptr<ModelLibraryLocal>>`. The cast only reinterprets the *outer* `shared_ptr`'s storage; the pointee is still a `list<shared_ptr<ModelLibraryLocal>>`, not a `list<shared_ptr<ModelLibrary>>`. `std::list<T>`'s node layout depends on `T`, so any caller doing `->size()`, iteration, or `front()/back()` on the returned list reads memory as a different type → garbage, desynchronized iterators, or crash. This is the core method returning all libraries to every consumer (including the new `ModelManager::getLibraries` consolidation, which iterates it).

**2. ModelLibrary.cpp:84–86 — null dereference of `model` in `getModelTree`.**
`auto model = ModelManager::getManager().getModel(getName(), uuid);` then `if (ModelManager::passFilter(filter, model->getType()))`. In external mode, `ModelManagerExternal::getModel` returns `nullptr` on `ModelNotFound`/`ConnectionError`, and the fallback `_localManager->getModel(uuid)` can also return null. If the uuid is from an external library whose fetch failed (or is a cached-negative entry), `model` is null → `model->getType()` is a null deref → crash when the tree is built.

**4. ModelManagerExternal.cpp:126–145 — data race on the shared static LRU cache.**
`getModel` reads/writes `_cache` (`contains`, `lookup`, `emplace`) with no lock, while `_mutex` is only ever held in `initCache` (47–57). With concurrent callers (UI thread + worker, or any thread calling the singleton), `contains/lookup/emplace` on the static `LRU::Cache` race → corrupted cache, wrong models, or crash. The declared static `_mutex` exists precisely to serialize this and is unused at the point of actual cache mutation.

**5. ModelManager.cpp:112–116 — external cleanup is unreachable dead code.**
```
return ModelManagerLocal::cleanup();
#if defined(BUILD_MATERIAL_EXTERNAL)
    if (_externalManager) { _externalManager->cleanup(); }
#endif
```
The unconditional `return` exits `cleanup()` first, so `_externalManager->cleanup()` never executes — external-side teardown never happens on shutdown regardless of `_useExternal`.

**6. ModelManagerExternal.cpp:141–144 — negative cache is never invalidated on transient `ConnectionError`.**
On `ConnectionError`, `getModel` `emplace`es a permanent `nullptr` for that uuid. The null is only erased by `addModel`/`migrateModel` for that exact uuid, and `ModelManager::refresh()` never touches this cache. A transient network blip during a lookup permanently removes that model from the tree (and `ModelManager::getModel` falls through / returns null → see #2) for the rest of the session until the process restarts.

**9. ModelLoader.cpp:121–124 — `static_pointer_cast<ModelLibraryLocal>` on an arbitrary base `shared_ptr<ModelLibrary>`.**
`getModelFromPath(std::shared_ptr<ModelLibrary> library, ...)` unconditionally does `std::static_pointer_cast<ModelLibraryLocal>(library)`. If any future caller (or the non-local path) passes a plain `ModelLibrary` (external), `static_pointer_cast` on the raw pointer is UB; downstream `ModelEntry` construction then operates on a wrong-typed object. Currently safe only because `_libraryList` happens to hold locals, but the function's own signature accepts the base type.

**10. ModelManager.cpp:88–96 / ModelLibrary.cpp — `strcmp` + non-atomic static `_useExternal`.**
`OnChange` compares `Reason` with `strcmp(Reason, "UseExternal")` and writes the static `bool _useExternal` from the observer callback with no lock, while the same static is read by every rule (`getModel`, `getLibraries`, `getModelTree`, …) on other threads. Concurrent read/write of the static bool is a data race; the observed behavior flips mid-iteration, so a single `getLibraries`/`getModelTree` call can mix external+local handling inconsistently.

**11. ModelManager.cpp:208–216 (`libraryModels`) — swallows `LibraryNotFound`/`InvalidModel` but lets `ConnectionError` escape.**
The external branch catches only `LibraryNotFound` and `InvalidModel`; `ModelManagerExternal::libraryModels` (ModelManagerExternal.cpp:114–118) doesn't catch anything, so a `ConnectionError` propagates up through `getModelTree`/callers with no local fallback — offline external mode raises instead of degrading to local, unlike every other external path in this diff which falls back gracefully.

**12. ModelManagerExternal.cpp:47–54 — cache capacity is applied without associating it with the actual access path, and a stale prefs value on re-init can shrink the cache below current content.**
`initCache` (`_cache.capacity(cacheSize)`) runs on every construction and each `refresh` rebuilds from `ModelCacheSize`; a prefs value lowered while the cache holds live `Model` objects reduces capacity and the LRU silently drops entries that the rest of the code assumes are present (e.g. a previously fetched external model now misses and re-fetches) — minor, but a concrete wrong-behavior edge.
